## Why This Is Asked

This tests end-to-end upgrade governance at scale: enforcing tenant isolation, cross-cluster canaries, and SBOM-based gates in production.

## Key Concepts
- Cross-cluster Argo Rollouts canary strategies

- SBOM integrity checks as upgrade gates
- Tenant isolation via SPIFFE IDs
- Central audit webhook for traceability

## Code Example
```yaml
# Argo Rollouts canary manifest (minimal)
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: cnf-rollout
spec:
  replicas: 2
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: cnf
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 10
      - pause: { duration: 300s }
```

```yaml
# Audit webhook payload (example)
tenant: tenant-A

```

- What metrics and alerting would you rely on for automatic rollback?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to design tenant-scoped runtime behavior using simple primitives (ConfigMap + sidecar) and validation via webhook, a common CNF pattern.

## Key Concepts
- Tenant isolation via per-namespace ConfigMap
- Runtime feature flags controlled by a sidecar
- Validation via admission webhook
- Minimal end-to-end test within one namespace

## Code Example
```yaml
# CNF feature flag ConfigMap
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-features
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  flags.json: |
    { "experimental": true }
```

```yaml
# CNF deployment with sidecar (simplified)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-app
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: cnf
        image: cnf:latest
        env:
        - name: tenantID
          value: "tenant-a"
      - name: feature-sidecar
        image: feature-sidecar:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: flags
          mountPath: /etc/cnf/flags.json
          subPath: flags.json
      volumes:
      - name: flags
        configMap:
          name: cnf-features
```
